title: Area-model division with a 2-digit divisor (`division:area_model_div_4by2` on the `area-model-div` cell)

template.also: the kit's long-division bracket (`bracketSvg`, `bracketLine` from `js/modules/sheet/cells/long-division.js`) for the `long` form; generator branches `area_model_div_2by1` / `area_model_div_3by1` in `js/modules/gen-operations.js` (the new `area_model_div_4by2` branch sits beside them and deals `long_div_2digit`'s 4-digit class); options `js/modules/skill-options.js` (`_amEdgesOpt`, `_amFormOpt`); `screen-cell.js` draws the same cell on the practice card, online worksheet and quiz (`_kitTwin`). The siblings 2by1 and 3by1 share the cell but are NOT on this card (open question 1)

summary: One boxed cell per problem: a rectangle split into two parts (the tens part and the ones part of the quotient times the 2-digit divisor, e.g. 1360 | 204), the divisor on its left side (printed, or a box on `amEdges: blank`), a box above each part for its side length (the partial quotient: 40, 6), and under it the problem in the form asked (1564 ÷ 34 = [ ], the long-division bracket with the quotient box over the dividend, or 1564 over 34) with the quotient box. Black line art, Andika at the digit size, the cell measured and never squeezed. Paper, key and the three screen hosts are one drawing (the existing cell, unchanged geometry; this card adds a skill, not a template).
teaches: 5.NBT.B.6 (M.EE.5.NBT.6): find whole-number quotients of 4-digit dividends and 2-digit divisors, illustrated with an area model: split the dividend into the tens part and the ones part of the quotient, find each side length from a 2-digit x multiple-of-ten fact, add them. Deals `long_div_2digit`'s 4-digit class (divisor 11-59 by default, 11-99 on the wider value; quotient 2-digit, exact). WRM Y6.B2.S11 (partial: the area model before the long-division layout). Not this card: remainders, the pupil choosing the split, 3-digit dividends, the siblings 2by1 / 3by1 (open questions).
research: design/research/area_model_div_4by2.md (2026-11-14). No premium logins this round: the memory file with the MathWorksheets4Kids / IXL credentials does not exist on this machine; MW4K's area-model pages were not reachable by URL (404) and IXL's "Divide using area models" (grade 5) is behind its sign-in. Public K5 Learning grade-5 division hub read (divisor bands 10-25 / 10-99, exact before remainder). Content model from the repo (PROBLEM_TYPES DV-07 / DV-11 / RL-17, ladder DL', the long_div_2digit P8 deal) and from publicly known site grammar; 24 sample items generated and read (L4).
problemTypes: DV-11 area model, parts given: the dividend split by the quotient's place value inside the rectangle; the pupil writes each side length (partial quotient) and the quotient - the core item
DV-11 with the divisor a box too (`amEdges: blank`), or mixed down the page (`mixed`)
the problem shown as the division sign, the long-division bracket (the bridge to DV-07 `long_div_2digit`) or a fraction (`amForm`)
NOT built here (section 9): the pupil chooses the split with friendly multiples (10x, 20x, 5x of the divisor); a remainder; a missing dividend or divisor
progression: divisor a multiple of ten, 20-90 (each side length a scaled fact: 70 x 30 = 2100) - `amDivisor: tens`
divisor 11-59 (the default; `long_div_2digit` at its default Max Number) - `amDivisor: 59`
the divisor a box too (`amEdges: blank`): the pupil reads the divisor off the problem
the bracket form (`amForm: long`) beside the model, then `long_div_2digit` itself

drawing.sizes: M and L only (owner 2026-11-13; S falls back to M). Digits 22 / 28 pt (tokens.js SIZES); answer strip SL-12 height; boxes at least 2 x Hw wide and as wide as the widest possible value (2 digits per partial quotient and quotient, never the answer's own length, L3). Part columns sized to 4 digits. Cell footprint (template `footprint()`, no browser): sign 94 x 58 mm at M, 116 x 66 mm at L; long + blank divisor 86 x 68 / 100 x 79 mm; `maxCols: 2`, `measure: true`.
notes: Payload (`q.cell = {template: 'area-model-div', v: 1, payload}`): `dividend`, `divisor`, `parts` [tens part, ones part], `form` ('sign' | 'long' | 'fraction'), `edges` ('given' | 'blank'), `uid`. Slots `q-0`, `q-1` (side lengths), `side` (blank divisor only), `total`. The generator never bakes HTML; `q.visual` is `_kitTwin('area-model-div', payload)`.

No template change is planned. If the measured cell does not fit two columns at M, the fix is in the template's column width rule (part columns from the widest part, not the widest possible 4-digit value), checked on 2by1 / 3by1 too so their pages do not move; never a smaller font (SCC-T4).
Key: every slot written (AK-1), reddish orange on keys only (INK-31). States blank / traced / answered / wrong share one geometry (SCC-T10); the screen twin's inputs ARE the slots (SCC-T15, L5).

A number-size band, so a plain option, not a preset skill (open question 3). Share codes: an appended option with the default 59, so codes decode unchanged.

openQuestions.q: The siblings `area_model_div_2by1` and `area_model_div_3by1` draw the same cell and have not passed the 8/10 redesign. Does this card (and its critic) cover them too?
openQuestions.recommended: No: this card covers the new skill only, so the round stays one skill. Add them to this card later with --resign when their own lane comes (copy-light review on a then-passed template).

openQuestions.q: Remainders: `long_div_2digit` is exact and the cell has no remainder slot. Offer a remainder value now?
openQuestions.recommended: No (hidden). Exact quotients only, as the problem class asked for. A remainder needs an `r` slot in the cell and is its own step (WRM Y6.B2.S12); propose it with long_div_2digit's remainders option later.

openQuestions.q: Is the divisor band `amDivisor` (tens / 11-59 / 11-99) a distinct difficulty that must also be a preset skill (CLAUDE.md 2026-10-17)?
openQuestions.recommended: No: it is a number-size band (a small tweak, like range), so a plain option. If the owner wants "Area model division by a multiple of ten" findable, it becomes the preset `area_model_div_4by2_tens` {amDivisor: 'tens'} with its own label, tags, terms and code.

openQuestions.q: Offer `constant` (Divide by: tick divisors) as on 2by1 / 3by1?
openQuestions.recommended: No: 89 ticks is not usable, and the band covers the need.

openQuestions.q: The pupil choosing the split (partial quotients with friendly multiples 10x, 20x, 5x; parts left blank) - an option here?
openQuestions.recommended: Not in this build (hidden). It is a new task with its own response (the parts written, then checked) and, by the distinct-option rule, a preset skill; propose it as a build-list entry after this skill passes.

openQuestions.q: Capacity: the footprint says 94 mm at M (two columns need about 91 mm) and 116 mm at L (one column). Accept M 1 x 4 and L 1 x 3 if the measured cell does not fit two columns?
openQuestions.recommended: Fit two columns at M first, by sizing part columns to the widest part dealt (not every possible 4-digit value) inside the template, re-checked on 3by1; accept L 1 x 3 (3 a page, like the other wide models). Never a smaller digit size.

openQuestions.q: MW4K / IXL research ran without logins (no credentials file on this machine). Sign now?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes; the content model is the long_div_2digit class plus DV-11, which the repo already decides. Re-sign only if logged-in research changes the problem types or the progression.
